items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: I had a really really strange experience with Big Mama Thornton down at the Cookery.

ctx.x: of lay persons knew me. But the guy that's the operator would be listening to modern musicians some and you know, and didn't hire me, but I would come, and they would think...because the man that owned that Popcorn Club said that I was the only one that at 2 o'clock, when the place was closing, the place was still packed and they were demanding encores. And those were his exact words.

I had a really really strange experience with Big Mama Thornton down at the Cookery. You know, she made "You Ain't Nothin' But a Houn' Dog," and she was really a strange person. But she knew...she knew the blues, you know.
I played that piano summit out at Waterloo Village last year.
